summary: Enhance your understanding of legal frameworks and gender-based violence with our comprehensive training course. Empower yourself to make a difference today.
lede: Gender-based violence legal frameworks training helps practitioners apply legal and policy duties when responding to cases. It is for police and justice personnel, health and social-service providers, and policy or program staff who need to interpret relevant provisions, document and refer cases, and protect survivor rights. Topics include reporting obligations, evidence integrity, confidentiality and consent, referral coordination, and survivor-centered procedures to avoid secondary victimization.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who interact with GBV survivors, influence GBV-related decisions, or shape policies and systems.
audience: Social workers, case managers, and GBV program
Human rights officers and gender focal points
Shelter, safe house, and crisis center managers
modules: Understanding Gender-Based Violence and the Law
National Legal Frameworks on Gender-Based Violence
Regional and International Instruments on GBV and Human Rights
Survivor-Centered and Rights-Based Approaches in Legal Practice
Reporting, Documentation, and Evidence in GBV Cases
Justice System Responses: Police, Prosecution, and Courts
Health, Social Services, and Multi-Sector Coordination
Workplace GBV, Harassment, and Safeguarding Frameworks
Barriers, Biases, and Gaps in GBV Legal Responses
Advocacy, Law Reform, and Strategic Use of Legal Frameworks
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of gender-based violence concepts and some professional experience in justice, social services, or a related field.
